STATEMENT L
August 9, 1973
1080-1-00 2015-1-00 CC: HNB HLF-ETB TZH ICH DE 9 HKB File
Mr. I. C. Herried Wisconsin Division of Highways Room 551 4802 Sheboygan Avenue Madison, Wisconsin
Dear Sir:
I have been a member of the Hamlin-Garland School District for five years. It is with deep sorrow that I look upon the construction of the Milwaukee Airport Spur. I don't think the road will be good for our neighborhood; it's going to hurt the school you know, and I can't understand what the benefits of it are.
I've read the impact statement. I don't understand too much of the technical details, but there were sections in the report which made me mad. It seemed to me that you were making overstatements about the project that were intended to mislead the public and justify it to those who weren't paying attention.
First of all, I don't think any of those bright engineers in your department have ever travelled on east College Avenue between the interchange and 6th Street. There are sections on that road that make travelling very difficult. On page 8 of the statement, it reads, "Diversion of airport-oriented traffic to the proposed new facility would allow the local street system to function at a desirable service level without extensive improvements." The only way I can figure this statement out is that the person who wrote it never travelled on College Avenue or he figures that once we get the airport spur, all of our highway and transportation problems will be solved for awhile. I'd prefer an improved College Avenue to the airport spur, if you're interested in my opinion.
My next complaint-comment is based on the information on page 32. You state that the projected growth of air passenger traffic will be from 1.6 million in 1968 to 5.4 million in 1990. This growth you state will make inefficient our present access ways to Mitchell Field. These figures and your predictions have no meaning for me until I know how many people will be transferring flights and how many will be travelling by road from the airport.
I also note that your population figures for southeastern Wisconsin are based on a study in 1967. I thought I remembered reading somewhere that all of these predictions were awash after the 1970 census. Am I right or wrong?
